method: CBOR is the Concise Binary Object Representation of RFC 8949. Decoding reads items from the first byte to the last: the first byte of each item carries a major type in its top three bits and additional information in the low five, so major types 0 and 1 are unsigned and negative integers (a negative integer n encodes the value -1 - n), 2 and 3 are byte strings and UTF-8 text strings, 4 and 5 are arrays and maps, 6 wraps a tag around one nested item, and 7 holds false, true, null, undefined, simple values and IEEE 754 binary16, binary32 and binary64 floats. Lengths and integer values below 24 sit in the header byte itself, and larger ones follow in 1, 2, 4 or 8 big-endian bytes; additional information 31 marks an indefinite-length string, array or map, which runs until a 0xff break byte. The page reports each item's byte offset and encoded length, validates UTF-8 strictly (rejecting overlong forms, surrogate code points, code points above U+10FFFF and cut-off sequences), and rejects truncation, reserved additional information 28 to 30, a break outside an indefinite item, indefinite strings whose chunks are not of the same major type, and simple values below 32 encoded as a following byte. Integers above 2^53 are shown as exact decimal strings because JavaScript numbers cannot hold them, and tags 2 and 3 whose payload is a byte string also show the decimal bignum value. Maps with text keys become JSON objects; maps with any other key type, or with a repeated key, are shown as an ordered $map list of pairs. Items that use more bytes than the shortest form are counted as non-minimal rather than rejected, and duplicate map keys, indefinite lengths, tags and the bignum note are listed per item, so the page inspects CBOR as it is rather than re-serialising it. Encoding parses a JSON value and writes canonical CBOR: the shortest integer form, definite lengths, UTF-8 text, 64-bit floats for non-integral numbers, and map keys ordered by encoded key length and then bytewise, the deterministic encoding of RFC 8949 section 4.2.1. Byte strings, tags, wide integers, undefined, simple values and special floats are written from the markers $bytes, $tag, $bigint, $undefined, $simple and $float, and $map writes an ordered map whose keys are not limited to text. Inputs are limited to 4,096 bytes, 2,000 items and 32 levels of nesting, and every value is computed in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
